text.opengl: Add the render loop: `while (!glfwWindowShouldClose(window))` that calls `glfwSwapBuffers(window)` and `glfwPollEvents()` every frame.

hint.opengl: Without a loop `main` ends straight away. `glfwPollEvents` processes the window's events (including the close button), `glfwSwapBuffers` shows the finished frame.

text.opengl: Make the viewport follow the window size: write `framebuffer_size_callback` (it calls `glViewport(0, 0, width, height)`), declare it at the top and register it with `glfwSetFramebufferSizeCallback`.

hint.opengl: The signature is `void framebuffer_size_callback(GLFWwindow* window, int width, int height)`. Register it right after `glfwMakeContextCurrent(window);`.

text.opengl: Close the window with Escape: write `processInput` (`glfwGetKey(window, GLFW_KEY_ESCAPE) == GLFW_PRESS` → `glfwSetWindowShouldClose(window, true)`), declare it, and call it at the start of every frame.
text.d3d12: Close the window with Escape: in `WindowProc`, handle `WM_KEYDOWN` and call `DestroyWindow(hWnd)` when `wParam == VK_ESCAPE`.

hint.opengl: Call `processInput(window);` as the first thing inside the render loop (it replaces the input TODO).
hint.d3d12: Add a `case WM_KEYDOWN:` that returns 0. Destroying the window sends `WM_DESTROY`, which posts `WM_QUIT`: the loop ends and `OnDestroy` waits for the GPU.

text.opengl: Clear the screen every frame: `glClearColor(0.2f, 0.3f, 0.3f, 1.0f);` then `glClear(GL_COLOR_BUFFER_BIT);`.
text.d3d12: Fill in `PopulateCommandList`: reset the allocator and the list, transition the back buffer `PRESENT` → `RENDER_TARGET`, clear its RTV with `{ 0.2f, 0.3f, 0.3f, 1.0f }`, transition it back to `PRESENT` and `Close()` the list.

hint.opengl: `glClearColor` only sets the colour (state); `glClear` does the clearing. Put both in the render section of the loop, before `glfwSwapBuffers`.
hint.d3d12: Store each barrier in a local `CD3DX12_RESOURCE_BARRIER barrier = CD3DX12_RESOURCE_BARRIER::Transition(...)` and pass `&barrier`. The RTV is `CD3DX12_CPU_DESCRIPTOR_HANDLE rtvHandle(m_rtvHeap->GetCPUDescriptorHandleForHeapStart(), m_frameIndex, m_rtvDescriptorSize)`.

text.vulkan: Create the window surface: add `VkSurfaceKHR surface;`, fill in `createSurface()` with `glfwCreateWindowSurface`, and destroy it with `vkDestroySurfaceKHR` in `cleanup()` (after the debug messenger, before the instance).

hint.vulkan: `glfwCreateWindowSurface(instance, window, nullptr, &surface)`; throw `"failed to create window surface!"` if it doesn't return `VK_SUCCESS`.

text.vulkan: Find a queue family that can present: add `presentFamily` to `QueueFamilyIndices` (and `isComplete()`), check `vkGetPhysicalDeviceSurfaceSupportKHR` in `findQueueFamilies()`, create one queue per unique family in `createLogicalDevice()` and get `presentQueue`.

hint.vulkan: The graphics and the present family are often the same index – a `std::set<uint32_t> uniqueQueueFamilies` avoids creating the queue twice.

text.vulkan: Check swap chain support: add `deviceExtensions`, `SwapChainSupportDetails`, `checkDeviceExtensionSupport()` and `querySwapChainSupport()`; make `isDeviceSuitable()` require them and enable the extension in `createLogicalDevice()`.

hint.vulkan: `vkGetPhysicalDeviceSurfaceCapabilitiesKHR`, `vkGetPhysicalDeviceSurfaceFormatsKHR`, `vkGetPhysicalDeviceSurfacePresentModesKHR` – the last two with two calls: count first, then the data.

text.vulkan: Create the swap chain: add its members, write `chooseSwapSurfaceFormat()` (`B8G8R8A8_UNORM`), `chooseSwapPresentMode()` (MAILBOX, else FIFO) and `chooseSwapExtent()`, fill in `createSwapChain()`, get the images, and destroy it in `cleanup()`.

hint.vulkan: Ask for `minImageCount + 1` images, use `VK_IMAGE_USAGE_COLOR_ATTACHMENT_BIT`, and `VK_SHARING_MODE_CONCURRENT` only if the two families differ. Then `vkCreateSwapchainKHR` and `vkGetSwapchainImagesKHR` twice.

text.vulkan: Create one `VkImageView` per swap chain image in `createImageViews()` (2D, the swap chain format, identity swizzle, colour aspect, 1 mip level, 1 layer); add `swapChainImageViews` and destroy them in `cleanup()`.

hint.vulkan: Resize `swapChainImageViews` to `swapChainImages.size()` and loop over the images.

text.vulkan: Create the render pass in `createRenderPass()`: one colour attachment (`loadOp = VK_ATTACHMENT_LOAD_OP_CLEAR`, `storeOp = STORE`, `UNDEFINED` → `PRESENT_SRC_KHR`), one subpass and the dependency on `VK_SUBPASS_EXTERNAL`; add `renderPass` and destroy it in `cleanup()`.

hint.vulkan: The attachment reference uses `VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_COLOR_ATTACHMENT_OPTIMAL`; both stage masks of the dependency are `VK_PIPELINE_STAGE_COLOR_ATTACHMENT_OUTPUT_BIT`.

text.vulkan: Create a framebuffer per image view in `createFramebuffers()` (the render pass, one attachment, the swap chain extent, 1 layer); add `swapChainFramebuffers` and destroy them in `cleanup()`.

hint.vulkan: Just like the image views: resize, loop, `vkCreateFramebuffer`.

text.vulkan: Create the command pool (`VK_COMMAND_POOL_CREATE_RESET_COMMAND_BUFFER_BIT`, graphics family) in `createCommandPool()` and allocate one primary command buffer in `createCommandBuffer()`; destroy the pool in `cleanup()`.

hint.vulkan: Command buffers are freed together with their pool, so only `vkDestroyCommandPool` goes in `cleanup()`.

text.vulkan: Write `recordCommandBuffer(VkCommandBuffer commandBuffer, uint32_t imageIndex)`: begin the command buffer, begin the render pass on `swapChainFramebuffers[imageIndex]` with the clear value `{{{0.2f, 0.3f, 0.3f, 1.0f}}}`, end the render pass and the command buffer.

hint.vulkan: The clear happens because of the render pass's `loadOp = CLEAR`; the colour comes from `renderPassInfo.pClearValues`. Nothing calls the function yet.

text.vulkan: Create the semaphores and the fence in `createSyncObjects()` and fill in `drawFrame()`: wait for and reset the fence, acquire an image, record the command buffer, submit it and present the image; destroy the sync objects in `cleanup()`.

hint.vulkan: Create the fence signalled, and one `renderFinishedSemaphores` entry per swap chain image. Order: `vkWaitForFences`, `vkResetFences`, `vkAcquireNextImageKHR`, `vkResetCommandBuffer`, `recordCommandBuffer`, `vkQueueSubmit`, `vkQueuePresentKHR`.

text.d3d12: Create an RTV descriptor heap with `FrameCount` descriptors, store `m_rtvDescriptorSize`, and create a render target view for each back buffer (`GetBuffer`, `CreateRenderTargetView`, `rtvHandle.Offset(1, m_rtvDescriptorSize)`).

hint.d3d12: Descriptors sit next to each other in the heap, `m_rtvDescriptorSize` bytes apart – ask the device with `GetDescriptorHandleIncrementSize(D3D12_DESCRIPTOR_HEAP_TYPE_RTV)`.

text.d3d12: Create the command allocator at the end of `LoadPipeline` (`CreateCommandAllocator`) and, in `LoadAssets`, the command list (`CreateCommandList`, with a null pipeline state) – then `Close()` it.

hint.d3d12: Both use `D3D12_COMMAND_LIST_TYPE_DIRECT`. A new command list is open for recording; the render loop expects it closed.

text.d3d12: Create the fence (`m_fenceValue = 1`) and the fence event in `LoadAssets`, fill in `WaitForPreviousFrame` (signal, wait with `SetEventOnCompletion` + `WaitForSingleObject`, update `m_frameIndex`) and `OnDestroy`.

hint.d3d12: `m_commandQueue->Signal(m_fence.Get(), fence)`, then `m_fenceValue++`; only wait if `m_fence->GetCompletedValue() < fence`. `OnDestroy` waits, then calls `CloseHandle(m_fenceEvent)`.

text.d3d12: Fill in `OnRender` (`PopulateCommandList()`, `ExecuteCommandLists`, `m_swapChain->Present(1, 0)`, `WaitForPreviousFrame()`) and call `app.OnUpdate(); app.OnRender();` from the main loop when `PeekMessage` finds no message.

hint.d3d12: Add an `else` branch to the `if (PeekMessage(...))`. `Present(1, 0)` waits for the next vertical blank (vsync).
